description.p: FileID tags, dedupes, restructures, and renames tens of thousands of files locally — no cloud, no telemetry. Point it at a folder and on-device AI sorts your photos, documents, and media: automatic content tags, face grouping for people, duplicate and near-duplicate cleanup, deep document analysis, and a butler-grade restructure that proposes a tidy folder tree you can preview before applying.

ul.li: Library — search by filename, tag, or extracted text; grid preview.
People — face clustering into named persons.
Cleanup — exact and perceptual near-duplicate detection.
Deep Analyze — opt-in vision-language analysis; requires a compatible external llama-mtmd-cli and is not yet available in the Flatpak sandbox.
Restructure — preview a proposed folder tree, then move or symlink.
Settings — pick models, tune thresholds, manage the local library.

description.p: The only network egress is user-initiated AI model downloads from huggingface.co. No analytics, crash reporting, or update pings — ever.

Fresh cross-platform functional baseline with all six native product areas, People naming and face reassignment parity, grounded Deep Analyze results, and native sleep inhibition for long-running scans.

The macOS scan sidebar now keeps counting, estimating, and time-left feedback visible throughout a scan. The macOS engine is packaged and launched as a background agent, preventing a second Dock application during local AI processing.

Face groups are no longer hidden by a size threshold. Merge suggestions reject people who appear together in the same photo, require per-pair review, and use the shared bounded engine path on Linux. Suggested-pair processing uses persisted centroids on macOS to reduce memory use, and stale suggestions are invalidated after every accepted merge.

People grouping and Restructure reliability. Faces are judged by pixel size instead of frame share, recovering real faces that were discarded; near-identical face groups now merge, so one person is no longer split across many groups; and People hides one-moment fragments while keeping every named group. Restructure Apply no longer abandons a whole batch over one changed file, states only the moves it will actually make, and keeps Undo available after a cancelled undo. Deep Analyze gains a folder-exclusion list.
Cross-platform release with hardened CLI/TUI workflows, packaging, and engine portability.
